rounds.fact: Digg pioneered the user-voted news-aggregation format years before Reddit took over that space, and a single controversial 2010 redesign is often cited as the reason it lost most of its audience.
RadioShack's website in the early 2000s tried to combine its parts-and-electronics heritage with early attempts at cell phone retail, a business mix that never quite gelled online.
Gizmodo's early scoops on unreleased Apple products, sometimes from leaked prototypes, made it one of the most closely watched (and occasionally legally threatened) tech blogs of the 2000s.
eBay started in 1995 as AuctionWeb, reportedly built to help the founder's fiancee trade Pez dispensers. By 1999 it was already a sprawling grid of category links and live auctions.
Airbnb started in 2008 with the founders renting out air mattresses in their own apartment during a design conference, which is where the original name came from.
